previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after falling at home, resulting in a closed medial tibial plateau fracture. Due to multiple comorbidities including morbid obesity, chronic heart failure, and HIV, surgical intervention was deemed high-risk, so the fracture was managed conservatively with a hinged knee brace and strict non-weight-bearing status. She remained stable throughout the hospitalization, with no complications. An asymptomatic urinary tract infection was treated with ciprofloxacin. Her chronic conditions, including HIV, asthma, and heart failure, were maintained on existing regimens without change. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with instructions for continued brace use, pain management, and follow-up care.

Somnolence: Improved HD2. It was thought to be due to multiple 
factors including pneumonia, recent uptitration of lithium, and 
possible component of hypoxia. ABG did not show significant 
hypercarbia. CXR shows RLL effusion +/-infiltrate. 
LFTs were normal except for slightly elevated T.bili. Lithium 
was restarted HD 2 at a lower dose than outpatient. We treated 
her PNA.

Healthcare associated RLL Pneumonia: Leukocytosis improved HD2 
after she received antibiotics. She received vancomycin and 
ceftriaxone and should continue a 7 day course of antibiotics. 
Sputum cx were sent and were negative for growth. Urine 
legionella antigen was negative. She received 
ipratropium/albuterol nebs, supplemental oxygen, and incentive 
spirometry. She was afebrile throughout her hospitalization.

Right pleural effusion: may have contributed to initial hypoxia. 
Improved with reinitiation of her outpatient diuretics. She was 
sating well on 2L of oxygen via nasal cannula on HD2.
.    
Depression/anxiety. We touched base with her outpt psychiatrist, 
Dr. ___ advised that we should restart lithium at 600mg 
QHS rather than at 1200mg QHS which was what she had been on 
outpatient.

HIV: Followed by Dr. ___. Currently with CD4 count 766 and 
undetectable viral load. Outpt HAART was continued: Ritonavir 
100 mg daily, Atazanavir 300 mg daily, emtricitabine/tenofovir 
200-300mg daily.  

s/p Tib/Fib Fracture: Patient has a history of fracture due to 
mechanical fall that was managed non-operatively. Tylenol was 
continued. After pt's mental status improved on HD2, methadone 
was restarted at a lower dose, 30mg TID, than her outpatient 
dose, 40mg TID. On HD3, she was restarted on her home dose of 
methadone. Neurontin was held while inpatient and should be 
restarted outpatient. Calcium & vitamin D, heparin for DVT 
prophylaxis were continued. NOPCO refitted her with a new brace 
prior to her discharge due to some pieces being missing from it. 
She will follow up with orthopedics outpatient. 

Hepatitis B, C. No evidence of decompensated cirrhosis on exam. 
Diuretics were initially held, restarted HD 2.
